title: Risk-Based Decision Making
metaDescription: Risk-informed decision frameworks that prioritize security and operations investment by consequence and likelihood, not by whoever asks loudest.
heroDek: Every security and operations budget is finite, and every stakeholder believes their request is the priority. GSS builds the risk-informed framework that ranks investment by consequence and likelihood, not by the loudest voice in the room.
contextHeading: Prioritization by advocacy is not a strategy
contextParagraphs: Without a shared framework, competing investment requests get resolved by whichever program has the most persuasive advocate, the most recent finding, or the most political capital — not by which gap actually carries the most consequence if left unaddressed. That produces a portfolio that looks responsive but isn't necessarily rational.

GSS builds risk-based decision frameworks that rank competing priorities on a consistent basis: consequence of failure, likelihood of occurrence, and cost and schedule to close the gap. The framework doesn't remove judgment from leadership — it gives leadership a common basis to apply that judgment against, so decisions are defensible to a board, a regulator, or an oversight body after the fact, not just at the moment they're made.

This capability sits downstream of the Optimization Assessment and KPI Development work: the same Best-in-Class gap analysis and indicator trends that identify where an organization is falling short become the inputs a risk-based framework ranks against each other.

methodology.label: Risk Criteria Definition
methodology.body: Consequence and likelihood scales are defined for the specific organization and mission before any request is scored against them.

methodology.label: Portfolio Intake
methodology.body: Competing investment requests, findings, and identified gaps are captured on a common basis, not compared informally between separate proposals.

methodology.label: Consequence & Likelihood Scoring
methodology.body: Each item is scored against the defined criteria, independent of which program or stakeholder submitted it.

methodology.label: Cost & Schedule Weighting
methodology.body: Cost and schedule to close each gap are factored against its risk score to surface the highest-value near-term actions.

methodology.label: Leadership Decision Framework
methodology.body: Results are presented in a format built for leadership decision-making — board-level or executive-level — not a raw spreadsheet.

methodology.label: Periodic Re-Scoring
methodology.body: The framework is re-run on a defined cycle so the portfolio reflects current conditions rather than a snapshot from the initial engagement.

faq.q: Does this replace our existing budget process?
faq.a: No, it feeds it. The framework produces a ranked, defensible prioritization that leadership carries into whatever budget or capital-planning process the organization already runs.

faq.q: Can this framework span both security and non-security investment?
faq.a: Yes — the consequence and likelihood criteria can be built to compare security, operations, and infrastructure investment on a common basis, which is often where the most value shows up.

faq.q: How often should the framework be re-run?
faq.a: Most organizations re-score on an annual cycle, or immediately after a material change — a new threat assessment, a significant finding, or a regulatory change.
